termsOfService.metaDescription: The rules between you, the event organizer and Vozko Tickets: purchase, payment, withdrawal, cancellation, entry and liability.
termsOfService.intro: These Terms govern access to and use of {productName}, a service provided by {legalName}. They apply both to people buying a ticket and to people publishing an event, and the obligations specific to each are identified. Nothing here removes a right that the Brazilian Consumer Code or another mandatory rule of law gives you.

summary.title: Summary of the main points
summary.content:
Art. 4, I of Decree 7.962/2013 requires the contract to be summarised before contracting, highlighting the clauses that limit rights. This summary serves that function and does not replace the full text.

• We provide the selling technology. The event is produced by the organizer, who answers for it. Section 5 sets out the exact division.
• The price shown at checkout is the total, and it has two parts: the ticket price, set by the organizer and owed to them, plus a service fee of 10 per cent on that amount, which is ours. Both appear on separate lines before you pay, and both come back in full on any refund.
• Payment is by PIX. Your tickets are held for a limited time and return to sale if the reservation expires.
• You have 7 days to withdraw from the purchase, counted from confirmation, with a full and immediate refund including any fee. That is art. 49 of the Consumer Code and there is no exception for proximity to the event.
• If the event is cancelled, postponed or materially changed, the choice between keeping the ticket and taking a full refund is yours, not ours.
• The account is for people aged 18 or over. A ticket for a minor is bought by an adult.
• Concession tickets and other statutory benefits are configured by the organizer and verified by the organizer at the entrance. Bring proof of your entitlement.

! Nothing in these Terms limits, excludes or reduces a right you hold under the Brazilian Consumer Code or another mandatory rule of law. Where a clause of these Terms conflicts with a protective rule, the rule prevails.

identification.title: Supplier identification
identification.content:
Art. 2 of Decree 7.962/2013 requires an e-commerce supplier to keep its full identification in a prominent and easily visible place. It is in the block at the foot of this page and in the footer of every page of the site.

• Business and registered name: {legalName}, with the company registration number and physical address given in the identification block.
• Electronic address for contractual contact: {supportEmail}.
• Data protection officer channel: {dpoEmail}.
• Corporate site: {siteUrl}.

The subject of the service is the provision of technology to publish events, create ticket tiers, control stock, take payment by PIX and record orders. The service is provided from Brazil, in Portuguese, English, German and Spanish, with prices in Brazilian reais.

For audiences in Germany and Spain, the information required by section 5 of the German Digital Services Act and by art. 10 of Spanish Law 34/2002 appears in the same identification block, permanently accessible.

definitions.title: Definitions
definitions.content:
These terms have the same meaning here and in the Privacy Policy.

• Platform: {productName}, including the website, the public event pages, the dashboard and the API serving those screens.
• Organizer: the account holder who registers and publishes an event and answers for staging it.
• Buyer: the person who acquires a ticket through the Platform.
• Consumer: a buyer who acquires as an end user, to whom the Brazilian Consumer Code applies in full.
• Tier: the ticket band created by the organizer, with its own price, quantity and sale status. It is what the dashboard calls a ticket.
• Order: the record of the purchase, with the chosen tiers, the amounts, the payment status and the buyer's details.
• Reservation: the temporary withdrawal of tickets from sale while the order is completed and paid.
• Payment institution: the authorised institution that issues and settles the charge, named at checkout.
• We: {legalName}. You: the person using the Platform, in whichever capacity they are using it.

acceptance.title: Acceptance, capacity and effect
acceptance.content:
By creating an account, accessing or using the Platform, you confirm that you have read and accept these Terms and the Privacy Policy. Both documents are reachable at any time from the footer and are presented, with a link, on the very screen where the account is created.

The account is for people aged at least 18 with civil capacity to contract. Age is verified against the date of birth given before a first purchase. A ticket intended for a minor is acquired by an adult on the minor's behalf, and that adult answers for the purchase.

If you act on behalf of a company or an organizer, you confirm that you have authority to bind it, and your acceptance binds it.

Under art. 46 of the Consumer Code, these Terms do not bind you if you were not given a prior opportunity to know their content. That is why the full text is public, with no account required, and is sent with the order confirmation in a medium that allows it to be stored and reproduced, as art. 4, IV of Decree 7.962/2013 requires.

roles.title: What we do and what the organizer does
roles.content:
The Platform is a technology supplier and a sales channel. It does not produce the event, is not a venue, does not engage the performers and does not run the door. The division below is factual and exists so that you know who to approach.

| Subject | Who answers |
| --- | --- |
| Operation of the site, the checkout and the charge | Us |
| The order record, the receipt and the purchase history | Us |
| Account security and protection of the data we process as controller | Us |
| The existence, content, date, venue and staging of the event | The organizer |
| Price, tiers, stock and the conditions of the offer | The organizer |
| Licences, permits, copyright, venue safety and insurance | The organizer |
| Age rating and the rules on admission of minors | The organizer |
| Concession tickets: categories, quota and verification at the entrance | The organizer |
| Entry, searches, venue rules and conduct at the event | The organizer |
| The event's refund policy and compliance with it | The organizer, with our operational support |

! This division describes facts and allocates obligations between us and the organizer. It is not, and cannot be read as, an exclusion or reduction of our liability towards a consumer. Suppliers forming part of the same supply chain are jointly and severally liable to the consumer under arts. 7, sole paragraph, 18, 20 and 25 of the Consumer Code, and that is how we treat our position. If you are a consumer with a complaint, you may bring it to us, and we will resolve it and settle up with the organizer afterwards.

accounts.title: Account, credentials and security
accounts.content:
The account is created and accessed with a single-use code sent to your email address. You may afterwards set a password as a second way in, and you may verify a phone number in order to receive the code over WhatsApp. The code is personal, short-lived and attempt-limited.

You must give true information, keep it up to date and protect access to your email address, your phone and your password. Credentials are personal and must not be shared. We never ask for your sign-in code through any channel: anyone who does is not us, and you should not give it to them.

Tell {supportEmail} immediately if you suspect unauthorised use. We end open sessions and, where necessary, invalidate access. Acts carried out by a valid session are attributed to the account, except where there are signs of fraud or where the law provides otherwise.

The same identification document cannot be linked to more than one account, so that per-person limits are not circumvented with a second account.

We may require verification of identity or of authority to represent where there is consistent evidence of fraud, of use of another person's document, or of risk to the operation.

organizer.title: The organizer's obligations
organizer.content:
This section binds whoever publishes an event. Any account holder may publish, and publication does not imply selection, curation, approval or any prior verification by us of the event or the organizer.

The organizer represents and warrants that: it has the capacity and authority to stage and promote the event; it holds the licences, permits and authorisations required, including operating, fire safety and health permits where applicable; it holds or has licensed the copyright, neighbouring rights and image rights in the content it publishes and in the programme, including any payments owed to collective management bodies; and it complies with the employment, tax and accessibility law applicable to the event.

The organizer is responsible for keeping accurate and current the name, description, date, time, venue, price, tier, stock, age rating, accessibility conditions, entry policy and refund policy. Incorrect information in an offer is the responsibility of whoever published it, and an offer binds the party that made it, under arts. 30 and 35 of the Consumer Code.

A material change to the event must be communicated to buyers clearly and in good time, and the organizer must inform us so that the support channels answer consistently. The organizer must keep sufficient funds to honour refunds, and indemnifies us for whatever we have to pay a consumer by reason of a fact attributable to the organizer, including costs, legal fees and administrative penalties.

The organizer may not publish a non-existent or unauthorised event, misleading information or unlawful content, and may not use a third party's trade mark, name or image without permission.

catalogue.title: Publishing the event, tiers and stock
catalogue.content:
The organizer registers the event, sets the venue and its map location, uploads images and video within the type, size and count limits shown in the dashboard, and creates as many tiers as it wishes, each with its own price, quantity and sale status.

An event begins as a draft and appears in the public area only once published. A tier sells only while it is on sale. Unpublishing an event removes it from the storefront and does not undo an order already paid: what has been sold remains owed to the buyer.

The Platform controls the stock of each tier and does not sell beyond the quantity available. A tier may sell out between your choosing it and completing the order, in which case the purchase does not complete and nothing is charged.

The conditions that govern your order are the ones published at the moment of purchase. Renaming a tier or changing its price afterwards does not alter an order already recorded.

purchase.title: How a purchase works
purchase.content:
A purchase has two stages, and the first already takes the tickets out of sale for you.

• You choose the tiers and quantities, and the tickets are reserved. The reservation is short and the page shows how long is left.
• You confirm your details and the reservation is extended for the payment period. A PIX charge is generated, with a copy-and-paste code and a QR code.
• You pay in your own bank application.
• Once payment is confirmed, the order becomes paid and you receive an email confirmation with the receipt and the event details.

If the reservation expires before payment, the tickets return to sale and the order closes with nothing charged. You may try again, subject to availability.

There is a limit on open orders per account and on tickets reserved per tier, shown on screen when reached. To free one up, complete or release an existing reservation.

Before confirming, you review the order summary and may correct the details you entered, as art. 4, II of Decree 7.962/2013 requires. Confirmation that your acceptance was received is sent by email, together with the text of these Terms, as items III and IV of the same article require.

The ticket gives the right of access described in the offer, on the conditions set by the organizer and the venue. Proof of your purchase is the paid order and the emailed confirmation, which carry the order reference. Entry is checked by the organizer, who may require official photographic identification matching the name on the order.

payments.title: Payment, price and what we never touch
payments.content:
The payment method is PIX, issued and settled by a payment institution authorised to operate by the Central Bank of Brazil and named at checkout. That institution acts as an independent controller of payment data, under its own terms and privacy policy.

! We never receive, transmit, process or store a card number, security code, magnetic stripe or chip data, banking password or banking credential. There is no card form in this application. Payment happens inside your own bank application, outside the Platform. We do not claim PCI-DSS certification, because we handle no card data and there is nothing to certify.

The price shown at checkout is the total payable, and it has two parts. The first is the ticket price, which the organizer sets and which is owed to them. The second is a service fee of 10 per cent calculated on that price, which is our remuneration for providing the Platform, processing the payment and keeping the record of the order. A ticket of R$ 100.00 is charged at R$ 110.00: the organizer receives the R$ 100.00 they set and the R$ 10.00 fee is ours. The fee is added to the price and not deducted from it, so the amount the organizer advertised is the amount the organizer receives.

The fee is calculated per ticket rather than on the order total, so that the price of one ticket multiplied by the quantity always equals the total charged. It is disclosed on the event page, before you choose, and again on a separate identified line in the order summary, before the payment step, in accordance with art. 2, IV and V of Decree 7.962/2013. In REsp 1.632.928 the Superior Court of Justice held that charging a fee on an internet ticket sale is lawful provided the amount is clear and accessible to the consumer, and that is the standard we follow: the obligation lies in the disclosure, and it is the disclosure we make prominently. A charge presented only inside a blind total is a practice we do not adopt.

There is no other charge of ours: we charge no delivery, printing, collection, issuing or instalment fee. The service fee is refunded in full, together with the ticket price, on every refund you are entitled to, including withdrawal under art. 49 of the Consumer Code and cancellation, postponement or material change of the event. We retain the fee in none of those cases.

A change to the fee is a material change to these Terms and follows section 26: it is announced at least 30 days in advance and does not apply retroactively to a purchase already completed. The amount charged on your order is the one in force and displayed when you bought.

A PIX refund is a return to the paying account, not a card reversal: there is no chargeback in PIX. We ask that the originating account be open to receive the return; if it has been closed, we will contact you at {supportEmail} to arrange another route. The time for the credit to arrive depends on the receiving institution.

If a payment arrives after a tier has sold out, the amount is refunded in full, because a ticket that no longer exists cannot be delivered.

withdrawal.title: Right of withdrawal
withdrawal.content:
! You have 7 days to withdraw from the purchase, counted from confirmation of the order, without having to give a reason. That is art. 49 of the Brazilian Consumer Code, which applies to every contract made away from business premises, including over the internet. On withdrawal, the amounts paid are returned in full and immediately, monetarily updated, including any fee that was charged. There is no minimum notice before the event and no other condition: we impose no cut-off for proximity to the date.

To withdraw, write to {supportEmail} from the account's email address quoting the order reference, or use the withdrawal option in your order history where it is available in your account. We confirm receipt of the withdrawal request immediately and instruct the return on the same business day. The credit reaching your account depends on the receiving institution's timing.

Withdrawal rescinds, at no cost, the contracts ancillary to that purchase, as art. 5 of Decree 7.962/2013 requires. No amount is retained as a fee.

After the 7 days, the art. 49 right of withdrawal no longer applies, but your rights in the event of cancellation, postponement, material change or failure of the service remain in full, and they are in the next section.

A different rule applies to consumers resident in the European Economic Area, which we state because it is less favourable and it would not be honest to omit it: the 14-day right of withdrawal does not apply to leisure services supplied on a specific date or period, which includes a ticket to an event with a fixed date, under art. 16(l) of Directive 2011/83/EU, section 312g(2) no. 9 of the German Civil Code and art. 103(l) of the Spanish consolidated consumer act. If you live in Brazil, the broader art. 49 applies, as described above.

cancellation.title: Cancellation, postponement and change of the event
cancellation.content:
An offer binds the party that made it. If the event does not happen as offered, the choice among the statutory alternatives is yours, and not the organizer's or ours, under arts. 20 and 35 of the Consumer Code.

| Situation | What you may choose |
| --- | --- |
| Event cancelled | full refund of the amount paid, monetarily updated |
| Postponed, with a new date announced | keep the ticket for the new date, or a full refund |
| Postponed with no new date | full refund |
| Change of venue or city, or material change to the programme | keep the ticket, or a full refund |
| Event only partly staged | proportional reduction of the price, or a refund |
| A failure of ours in the sales service | re-performance of the service, an updated refund, or a proportional reduction |

A refund covers the amount actually paid, not only the ticket's face value: where the failure is the supplier's, any fee charged also comes back. We do not impose credit, a voucher or a compulsory exchange in place of money. Law 14.046/2020, which during the pandemic allowed rebooking and credit instead of a refund, is no longer in force, and the general rules of the Consumer Code apply again in full.

Unforeseeable events and force majeure may justify not staging the event and may remove any duty to compensate additional loss, but they do not extinguish the return of what you paid for something you did not receive.

The organizer must communicate the change and provide the funds for refunds. We operate the return and follow it to completion. If you are a consumer, you do not have to settle this between the two of us: contact {supportEmail} and we will handle it.

meiaEntrada.title: Concession tickets and statutory benefits
meiaEntrada.content:
Law 12.933/2013 and its decree guarantee half-price admission to students, to people with disabilities and a companion where one is needed, and to low-income young people registered in the federal social register. The Elderly Persons Act, Law 10.741/2003, independently guarantees a 50 per cent discount and priority access to people aged 60 or over. State and municipal laws may widen the categories.

The Platform lets the organizer create reduced-price tiers, including half-price ones. The party that defines the categories, the price, the quantity set aside for the benefit and compliance with the statutory quota is the organizer, who represents and warrants that it does so in accordance with federal law and with the local law applicable to the municipality of the event.

! Proof of entitlement is checked at the entrance to the event, by the organizer, and not at the point of purchase. Buy a concession ticket only if you belong to one of the categories and can prove it. If the condition is not proved, the organizer may require payment of the difference or refuse admission, and that consequence follows from the law creating the benefit, not from a condition imposed by us.

The documents accepted are those the rule on the benefit specifies, and the organizer should not demand any beyond them: a national-standard student identification card showing name, date of birth, photograph, institution, level of study and validity, for students; official photographic identification, for people aged 60 or over; documentary proof of the disability together with official photographic identification, and proof of the companion's role where applicable; and the national youth identity card together with official photographic identification, for low-income young people.

We do not collect, request or keep proof of entitlement, medical reports, certificates or accessibility documents. Those are presented at the door and stay with you.

The organizer answers to you and to consumer protection bodies for configuring the benefit and the quota correctly, and indemnifies us for any penalty arising from a configuration it made.

entry.title: Entry to the event
entry.content:
Entry is run by the organizer or by the venue. Bring the order reference, which appears in the emailed confirmation, and official photographic identification. The organizer may check that the name on the document matches the one on the order, and may refuse admission to anyone who cannot show entitlement.

The venue's rules, including opening times, searches, prohibited items, capacity and conduct, belong to the organizer and the venue, and you accept them on entering. Refusal of admission for breaching those rules, for intoxication, for carrying a prohibited item or for conduct endangering other people does not give rise to a refund.

The age rating and the rules on admission of children and adolescents are declared by the organizer and checked by the organizer at the door, in accordance with the Brazilian Child and Adolescent Act and any order of the local juvenile court. Check those conditions before buying: refusal of admission to a minor for breach of the declared rule is a situation the organizer must address, and we support that.

Accessibility at the venue, including wheelchair spaces, companion seating and priority service, is an obligation of the organizer and the venue. If the offer advertised an accessibility condition that was not delivered, that is a failure to honour the offer, and section 12 applies.

transfer.title: Transfer and resale
transfer.content:
The Platform does not currently offer a mechanism for transferring a ticket between people, nor an official resale channel. An order stays linked to the account that placed it and to the document recorded in it.

You may not resell a ticket bought here above its price, advertise it on a resale channel, or buy tickets in volume for resale. Automated buying, use of bots, creating multiple accounts and using another person's document to circumvent a per-person limit are prohibited.

A ticket obtained or transferred in breach of this section may be invalidated, with the order cancelled and the amount returned to the original payer, and the account involved may be suspended. We do not cancel the ticket of somebody who bought in good faith without first attempting contact through the support channel.

If you need to transfer a ticket for a legitimate reason, write to {supportEmail} before the event. We assess it case by case with the organizer; there is no automatic right of transfer.

acceptableUse.title: Prohibited use
acceptableUse.content:
It is prohibited to use the Platform for fraud, money laundering, unlawful resale, a non-existent or unauthorised event, infringement of a third party's rights, unlawful, misleading or discriminatory content, distribution of malware, or improper collection of data.

It is also prohibited to circumvent a technical limit, to test for vulnerabilities without prior written authorisation, to automate access abusively, to scrape content at scale, to overload the infrastructure, to copy the service, to use a third party's trade mark without permission, and to access another party's account, audience or channel without valid authorisation.

We may remove content, limit operations and suspend access in order to prevent harm, comply with the law or investigate consistent evidence of abuse, with notice and an opportunity to put things right where that is reasonable and the urgency allows.

Good-faith security research is welcome at {supportEmail}: describe the finding, do not access third-party data beyond what is needed to demonstrate it, do not degrade the service, and give us a reasonable period before publishing. We do not treat a report made on those terms as a breach.

Disputing a charge with your bank or with a consumer protection body is not prohibited use, and we will not treat it as a breach. Repeated use of disputes to obtain access without paying may, on the other hand, lead to invalidation of the order and review of the account.

notice.content:
To report a non-existent or fraudulent event, unlawful content, copyright infringement, or misuse of a trade mark or image, write to {supportEmail} naming the page, describing the problem and its legal ground and, if you are the rights holder, providing proof of title and your contact details.

We examine the report and act according to the seriousness and the clarity of the illegality. integrations.title: Integrations and third-party services

suspension.content:

privacyPolicy.metaDescription: What data Vozko Tickets processes, on what legal basis, who it is shared with, where it goes and how long it is kept.

It is written to be read, not merely accepted. The Portuguese text prevails for data subjects in Brazil.

summary.title: One-minute summary
summary.content:
This summary guides the reading. It does not replace the sections below, which are the ones that govern.

• For the operation of your account, we are the controller. For the data an organizer enters about their own event, we are the processor and the organizer is the controller.
• We ask for an email address to create the account and, before your first purchase, your full legal name, a tax identification document and your date of birth. The document is required to issue the PIX charge, to verify the minimum age and to stop two accounts sharing one document.

• We do not use your data to train artificial intelligence models.
• You may exercise every right under the LGPD, and under the GDPR where it applies, by writing to {dpoEmail}.

controller.title: Who the controller is and how to reach them
controller.content:
The controller of the data processed to provide {productName} is {legalName}. Its registered name, company registration number and full address appear in the identification block at the foot of this document and in the footer of every page. The corporate site is {siteUrl}.

The channel for the data protection officer, required by art. 41 of the LGPD and by ANPD Resolution 18/2024, is {dpoEmail}. Use it to exercise rights, to ask about this Policy, to request the full text of the standard contractual clauses used for international transfers, or to raise a concern. For data subjects in the European Economic Area, the representative required by art. 27 of the GDPR is named in the identification block. The representative is not the data protection officer, holds a distinct function, and may be addressed in place of the controller by European authorities and by data subjects resident in the European Union.

This Policy covers the website, the public event pages, the organizer dashboard, the API serving those screens, and support. It does not cover an organizer's own website, the payment institution, which acts as an independent controller under its own terms, or any third-party service you reach from a link of ours.

roles.title: When we are controller and when we are processor
roles.content:
Art. 9, VI of the LGPD requires it to be clear who answers for which processing. On this platform the role changes with the data, and the table below is the complete map.

| Processing | Our role | Who decides the purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account, authentication, sign-in code, sessions | Controller | Us |
| Tax identification required in order to buy | Controller | Us, under legal and contractual duty |
| Order, PIX charge, refund, reconciliation | Controller | Us |
| Security records, anti-fraud limits, access logs | Controller | Us |
| Support and customer service | Controller | Us |
| Event name, description, venue, prices and media | Processor | The organizer |
| Buyer data the organizer consults in the dashboard | Processor | The organizer |
| An organizer's own messaging to their audience | Processor | The organizer |
| Payment data held at the payment institution | None: independent controller | The payment institution |

Where we are the processor, we handle the data on the organizer's documented instructions, as art. 39 of the LGPD requires, and we do not use it for an incompatible purpose of our own. If an instruction appears unlawful to us, we tell the organizer and may refuse it.

There is one activity where the decision is genuinely shared, and we would rather say so than leave it out: the ticket purchase contract itself. We define the checkout flow, the mandatory fields, the per-account limits and the transaction record; the organizer defines the event, the price and the entry conditions. In that specific activity, and only there, we are joint controllers with the organizer under art. 26 of the GDPR where it applies. The essence of the arrangement is this: we inform you at checkout and answer for the transaction data, the organizer informs you in its own notice and answers for the event, and you may exercise your rights against either of us without needing to know how the work is divided between us.

data.content:
This is the central table of this Policy. Each row is a purpose rather than merely a category, because legal basis is determined per purpose. The periods are the ones we apply; the retention section explains the exceptions that can extend them.

You do not need to give a name, a document or a date of birth to create an account and browse. You need them to complete a purchase. Declining has no consequence other than that the order cannot be completed.

sensitive.title: Sensitive data, and data we do not collect
sensitive.content:
We do not ask for sensitive data within the meaning of art. 11 of the LGPD or art. 9 of the GDPR. We do not collect racial or ethnic origin, religious belief, political opinion, trade union membership, health data, sex life, genetic data or biometric data.

A tax number, a passport number, a legal name and a date of birth are not sensitive data as legally defined, but they are high-value identifiers for fraud and we treat them with the care owed to sensitive data: they are encrypted at rest and the interface never displays the document in full.

• We never receive a card number, security code, magnetic stripe or chip data, banking password or banking credential, at any point and by any route. There is no card form in this application.
• We do not collect the home address of a natural person. The addresses we process are event venues, supplied by the organizer.
• We do not use the browser geolocation interface and do not collect precise device location.
• We do not collect children's data, and we do not process concession proof, medical reports, certificates or accessibility documents: that verification, where it happens, is carried out by the organizer at the venue entrance.
• We do not perform facial recognition or any form of biometric identification.

If an organizer includes sensitive data in an event description or image, that is their decision, they are the controller of that content, and they answer for the corresponding legal basis.

sources.title: Where the data comes from
sources.content:
Most of it comes from you, directly: when you create the account, when you complete your profile before a first purchase, when you register an event, when you upload an image and when you contact support.

Another part is generated by use, without your typing it: IP address, browser identification, access timestamp, error records and performance counters.

We receive data from third parties in three situations, and art. 14 of the GDPR requires the source to be disclosed:

• From the payment institution: the status of the charge, its identifier and the settlement date.
• From the organizer: the data they enter about the event and, where applicable, about their own team.
• From address services: when you type a postcode or search for an address in the event form, the query goes to a public address service, which returns street, city and coordinates.

We do not buy lists, we do not enrich records with third-party data, and we do not use social login.

cookies.title: Cookies and storage in your browser
cookies.content:
This application has no advertising cookie, no analytics cookie, no social network pixel and no third-party measurement script. There is no product telemetry, no session recording and no A/B testing tool. That is why there is no consent banner: there is no non-essential processing to consent to.

| Name | Function | Type | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| accessToken | keep the session authenticated | necessary | 15 minutes |
| refreshToken | renew the session without a new sign-in | necessary | 30 days |
| userData | show your name, email and role in the interface | necessary, accessible to the page you open | 30 days |
| NEXT_LOCALE | remember the language you chose | necessary | 1 year |
| theme | remember light or dark mode, in local storage | functional | until you clear the browser |
| dashboard preferences | remember the collapsed menu and the last area opened, in local storage | functional | until you clear the browser |

! The userData cookie contains your name, your email address and your role, and is accessible to the page you open. The session cookies are not accessible to scripts.

Blocking the necessary items prevents signing in and using the dashboard. If we ever introduce non-essential measurement or marketing, we will ask for consent first, with a clear way to refuse and to withdraw, following the ANPD guidance on cookies and, for anyone in the European Union, art. 5(3) of Directive 2002/58.

browserCalls.title: Requests your browser makes to third parties
browserCalls.content:
Some screens load resources served by third parties. In those cases your browser speaks to them directly, and your IP address is visible to that third party even though we send them nothing. We would rather state this than leave it implicit.

• The map on the public event page: map tiles are served by an open map provider. When you open an event page that has a location, your browser requests those tiles and the provider sees your IP address.
• Address lookup in the event form: as an organizer types an address, queries go to a geocoding service, which sees the IP address of whoever is typing.
• Postcode lookup: the query is addressed to a public address service, which sees the network address it comes from.

Typefaces are served from our own domain rather than by an external provider, precisely so that reading a page does not generate a request to a third party.

None of these requests carries your name, your email address, your document or your account identifier.

bases.title: Legal bases and the legitimate interest assessment
bases.content:
The legal basis for each purpose is in the table in section 4. Performance of a contract covers most of the service; compliance with a legal obligation covers the retention of access logs and the tax and consumer-law periods; legitimate interest covers security, fraud prevention and technical maintenance.

Where we rely on legitimate interest, we have run the three-stage assessment set out in the ANPD guidance and in art. 6(1)(f) of the GDPR: the purpose is to keep the platform secure and available; the necessity follows from there being no less intrusive way to detect credential reuse, reservation abuse and payment fraud; and the balancing rests on concrete safeguards, namely that the data is minimal, the period is short, there is no profiling, there is no automated decision about personal characteristics, and there is no advertising use. You may object to any processing based on legitimate interest by writing to {dpoEmail}.

We do not rely on legitimate interest for marketing, because we do not carry out marketing through this platform. We do not rely on consent as a general basis for the service, because consent asked for something indispensable is not freely given. Where consent is the basis, it will be specific, prominent and revocable at any time, and withdrawal does not invalidate processing already carried out.

transfers.title: International transfers
transfers.content:
Some of the suppliers above process data outside Brazil. Art. 14 of ANPD Resolution 19/2024 requires those transfers to be described in plain and easily accessible language, which is what the table in the previous section does, column by column: where it goes, what for, and under which mechanism.

The form of the transfer is the sending of strictly necessary fields for the contracted function, for as long as the supplier performs it, for the specific purpose stated in the table. The current destination countries are the United States and countries of the European Union, together with the global content delivery network used to serve images and maps.

For destinations in the European Union and the European Economic Area the mechanism is an adequacy decision, under art. 33, I of the LGPD. Since ANPD Resolution 32/2026 and Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/179, Brazil and the European Union recognise each other as adequate, and those transfers require no additional contractual clause. For all other destinations, including the United States, we adopt the ANPD standard contractual clauses in full and unaltered, as set out in Annex II to Resolution 19/2024, together with an assessment of the legal regime of the destination country.

You have the right to receive the full text of the clauses applicable to your situation. Write to {dpoEmail} and we will answer within 15 days, as art. 17 of that Resolution requires, subject to trade secrecy. Onward transfers, made by a supplier to a sub-processor of its own, are contractually subject to the same obligations and the same mechanism.

You may petition the ANPD about any transfer described here and, if you are in the European Union, the supervisory authority of your own country.

retention.title: Retention and erasure
retention.content:
The periods by purpose are in the table in section 4. This section explains where they come from and what can extend them.

Once the period ends, the data is erased or anonymised. It may be kept beyond that only on the grounds in art. 16 of the LGPD: compliance with a legal or regulatory obligation, the regular exercise of rights including in legal proceedings, and exclusive use by the controller in anonymised form. Fraud prevention and the investigation of an incident also support retention, for the duration of the investigation.

Backups may hold a record for a short interval after erasure, until those media rotate normally. Deleted media leaves storage immediately but may remain reachable through the content delivery network until the temporary copy expires.

security.title: Security
security.content:
We apply technical and administrative security measures proportionate to the risk, as art. 46 of the LGPD and art. 32 of the GDPR require. In terms that matter to you, this is what is committed.

• A password and a sign-in code are never stored in readable form, only irreversibly. The sign-in code has a short validity, an attempt limit and a send limit.
• Identification document, legal name, date of birth and phone number are encrypted at rest. The interface never displays the document in full, and the event organizer has no access to those fields.
• Account access runs through a session with a fixed duration, which can be revoked, and traffic is protected by TLS.
• We apply attempt and usage limits to contain abuse, account enumeration and fraud.
• Media upload is restricted to defined types and sizes.
• We store no card data, banking password or banking credential.

We do not claim ISO 27001 certification or a SOC 2 report, because we do not hold them. No system is invulnerable: use a strong password, do not reuse credentials, and tell {dpoEmail} about suspicious activity. We never send a request for a password, a full document number or banking data by email or message, and we never ask for your sign-in code: anyone who does is not us.

incidents.title: Security incidents
incidents.content:
An incident, as defined in art. 3, XII of ANPD Resolution 15/2024, is a confirmed adverse event affecting the confidentiality, integrity, availability or authenticity of personal data.

Where an incident may give rise to relevant risk or damage within the meaning of art. 5 of that Resolution, we notify the ANPD and the affected data subjects within 3 business days of confirming that personal data was affected. The communication to the data subject is written in plain language and, wherever possible, delivered individually and directly, and it states the nature of the data, the risks and possible impacts, the measures taken, the date we became aware, and the contact for the data protection officer. Because we hold tax identification documents and payment references, our working assumption is that the threshold of relevant risk will be met in most cases, rather than the reverse.

Where data subjects in the European Union are affected, we notify the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours under art. 33 of the GDPR, and we inform the data subjects where there is a high risk, under art. 34.

We keep a register of every incident, including those not communicated and the reasons for not communicating them, for at least 5 years, as art. 10 of the same Resolution requires.

Where an incident affects data for which we are the processor, we notify the controlling organizer without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of confirmation, so that they can meet their own deadline, and we assist with containment, investigation and any communications owed.

automated.title: Automated decisions and profiling
automated.content:
Art. 20 of the LGPD and art. 13(2)(f) of the GDPR require you to know what automation affects you. It is this: a reservation expires when its time runs out and the tickets return to sale; there is a cap on open orders per account and on reserved tickets per tier; one identification document cannot be linked to two accounts; and the order status follows the payment institution's confirmation of the charge.

These rules apply the same criterion to everyone, consider only data from the transaction itself, and do not assess you. There is no credit scoring, no risk score based on personal characteristics, no behavioural profiling, no targeted advertising and no automated decision evaluating your personality, your behaviour or your economic situation within the meaning of art. 20 of the LGPD and art. 22 of the GDPR.

Even so, if one of those automatic rules affects you and you want it reviewed, write to {dpoEmail}. A person examines the case, states the criterion applied and, where appropriate, undoes the effect. You do not need to demonstrate an error in order to ask for the review.

We do not use personal data processed on this platform to train, fine-tune or evaluate any artificial intelligence model, whether our own or a third party's.

rights.title: Your rights and how to exercise them
rights.content:
Art. 18 of the LGPD guarantees the rights below, and art. 9, VII requires them to be listed expressly rather than by cross-reference. For anyone in the European Union, arts. 15 to 22 of the GDPR guarantee equivalent rights, with the differences noted.

| Right | What it means | Response time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Confirmation and access | learn whether we process your data and obtain a copy | immediately in simplified form, or a full statement within 15 days |
| Correction | correct incomplete, inaccurate or out-of-date data | 15 days |
| Anonymisation, blocking or erasure | as to data that is unnecessary, excessive or processed unlawfully | 15 days |
| Portability | receive the data in a structured format, or have it sent to another supplier | 15 days, under the applicable regulation |
| Erasure of data processed on consent | delete what rested on your consent alone | 15 days |
| Information about sharing | learn who we share with and why | 15 days |
| Information about refusing consent | learn what happens if you decline | immediately |
| Withdrawal of consent | withdraw consent, without retroactive effect | immediately |
| Objection | object to processing based on legitimate interest or on a consent exemption | 15 days |
| Review of an automated decision | ask for a person to review it | 15 days |
| Restriction of processing, under the GDPR | limit use while accuracy or an objection is being resolved | 1 month, extendable by 2 |

Send the request to {dpoEmail}. It is free of charge. We may ask for additional information to confirm that you are who you say you are, but only what is strictly necessary: we do not ask for a photograph of a document or a selfie in order to answer an access request. If we refuse, in whole or in part, we state the ground and what you can do next.

An erasure request does not reach what the law requires us to keep: access logs for the statutory period, tax and accounting records, data needed to defend a legal claim, and incident records. In those cases we erase what can be erased and explain what remains, for how long and on what ground.

You may complain directly to the Brazilian data protection authority, to consumer protection bodies including Procon and the consumidor.gov.br platform, and, if you are in the European Union, to the supervisory authority of your country of residence under art. 77 of the GDPR. Complaining to an authority does not depend on contacting us first, but starting at {dpoEmail} is almost always faster.

communications.title: Messages we send
communications.content:
Today we send exactly three kinds of message, all transactional, each triggered by something you did:

• the sign-in code, by email or WhatsApp, when you ask to sign in;
• the pending charge notice, with the PIX code and the reservation deadline, when you complete an order;
• the payment confirmation, with the receipt and the event details, when the charge settles.

We send no newsletter, no promotion, no abandoned-basket recovery and no message about an event you did not buy. There is no marketing list on this platform and therefore nothing to unsubscribe from.

! A transactional message has no unsubscribe. It is part of performing the purchase: without the sign-in code you cannot get in, and without the confirmation you have no receipt. If you do not want to receive them, the route is not to complete the purchase, or to close the account.

If we ever begin sending marketing communications, they will depend on a specific and prominent indication from you, will carry one-click unsubscribe in every message, will respect the Brazilian do-not-disturb register and the telecommunications regulator's rules, and the consent will be revocable at any time. Marketing over WhatsApp will additionally follow Meta's Business Messaging Policy, including correct categorisation of the message template. None of this is active, and this Policy will be updated before it is.

Where an organizer sends communications to their own audience using a tool of ours, they are the controller of that communication, they answer for the legal basis covering each recipient, and we act as processor.

children.title: Children and adolescents
children.content:
An account on this platform is for people aged 18 or over. The age is genuinely checked against the date of birth given before a first purchase, not by a tick box: anyone under 18 cannot complete the registration that enables purchasing.

That choice is deliberate. A ticket for a minor is bought by an adult on their behalf, which is how the door works in any case. As a result we do not process children's or adolescents' data in order to operate accounts, and we do not depend on the guardian consent required by art. 14, para. 1 of the LGPD, nor on the age of consent in art. 8 of the GDPR, nor on the guardian-linked account regime of Law 15.211/2025.

We do not, under any circumstances, carry out profiling, segmentation or targeted advertising towards anyone identified as under 18.

Events may admit children and adolescents, and that is the organizer's decision. The organizer is responsible for declaring the age rating, the rule on accompaniment by a guardian and any requirement for judicial authorisation, for disclosing them before purchase and for verifying them at the entrance, in accordance with the Brazilian Child and Adolescent Act. If an organizer collects a minor's data in order to run the event, they are the controller of that data, must observe the child's best interest and must present their own privacy notice.

A legal guardian who wishes to access, correct or erase a minor's data that has reached us may write to {dpoEmail}, and the request is handled as a priority.

organizerData.title: Data under the organizer's control
organizerData.content:
Where your request concerns a specific event, a guest list or your attendance at an event, the party deciding the purpose is normally the organizer, and the request should go to them first. Their privacy notice is what governs that processing.

If you come to us anyway, we forward the request to the organizer within 5 business days and tell you that we have done so, identifying them. Where we act as processor, we give the technical assistance needed for them to answer you. None of this removes your right to address us about what is ours, nor, in the jointly controlled activity described in section 3, your right to bring the request against either of us.

The organizer, for their part, undertakes in the Terms of Service to present their own privacy notice, to collect only what is necessary, to have a legal basis, to set retention, to answer data subjects, and not to use data obtained through the platform for a purpose incompatible with the one that justified it.

photography.title: Photography and filming at the event
photography.content:
Recording image and sound at the venue is the activity of the organizer or of whoever they authorise, and not ours. The organizer is the controller of that processing, sets the legal basis, answers for signage at the venue and for advance notice to the public, and answers to a heightened standard where a child or adolescent appears.

The platform stores and serves the images and video the organizer uploads to promote the event. In that role we are the processor: we do not choose the content, we do not recognise people and we do not index faces.

If you appear in an image published on an event page and want it removed, write to {dpoEmail} naming the page and, if you can, the position in the image. We remove it or forward the request to the organizer according to each party's role, and we tell you what was done. Image rights are protected by art. 20 of the Brazilian Civil Code and, as to minors, by art. 17 of the Child and Adolescent Act, independently of whether there is a legal basis for the rest of the processing.

regional.title: Regional notes
regional.content:
The service is operated from Brazil, charges in Brazilian reais and uses PIX as its payment method. The LGPD is the primary regime.

For data subjects in the European Economic Area, including Germany, the GDPR applies to the extent that we offer the service to you: the legal bases in the corresponding column of the table in section 4 apply, as do the art. 27 representative named in the identification block, the rights in arts. 15 to 22, the one-month period extendable by two under art. 12(3), and the right to complain to the supervisory authority of your own country under art. 77. Because we have no establishment in the European Union, there is no lead authority and no one-stop shop: the competent authority is the one in your own country of residence.

For data subjects in Spain and in Spanish-speaking Latin America, the Spanish version of this Policy is the reference text, and the Spanish data protection agency is the competent authority for residents of Spain.

We publish this Policy in Portuguese, English, German and Spanish. The Portuguese version is authoritative for data subjects in Brazil, as art. 31 of the Consumer Code requires. For consumers resident in Germany and Spain, the version in that country's language prevails, and no language precedence clause removes from you the protection of the mandatory law of your country of habitual residence.

changes.title: Changes to this Policy
changes.content:
The version and the two dates at the top of the page identify the text: the effective date is when the version began to apply, and the updated date is when the text last changed. The two do not necessarily coincide, and the effective one governs.

A material change, such as a new purpose, a new legal basis, a new supplier with access to personal data, a new destination country or a longer retention period, is announced at least 30 days in advance, by email to account holders and by a notice in the product, before it takes effect. A correction to wording, to a legal reference or to contact details may be published immediately.

If a change would mean processing for a purpose incompatible with the one that justified collection, we will tell you in advance and prominently, and you may withdraw consent or object, under art. 9, para. 2 of the LGPD.

Previous versions are archived and supplied to anyone who asks at {dpoEmail}, together with a note of what changed between them.

When you write, describe the request and the context, and do not attach a password, a full card number or a photograph of a document: we do not need any of that to locate your relationship with us, and asking for excessive data in order to answer a privacy request would be the obvious contradiction.
